title: Model Churn Forecast & Competitive Opportunity Dashboard
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: Build a repeatable, data-driven dashboard and accompanying scoring system that forecasts model availability churn (likelihood a model or variant becomes unavailable, throttled, or materially repriced) and surfaces near-term competitive opportunities for product teams and procurers. The tool will combine public vendor signals, internal usage telemetry, pricing trend feeds, and qualitative research to produce a prioritized list of models to onboard, hedge, or deprecate.

Why: Engineering teams repeatedly scramble when a model becomes unreliable or unexpectedly expensive. Current ad-hoc monitoring flags outages but not the upstream risk of supply changes nor the scoring of viable substitutes. This initiative reduces surprise migrations, shortens procurement cycles, and converts model market dynamics into prioritized, operational work for product and infra.

Scope: Prototype dashboard + automated weekly churn scores for ~40 models (open and vetted closed variants), an API endpoint for teams to query scores, a one-page runbook for when a model crosses risk thresholds, and a lightweight experiment to surface suggested substitutes with expected latency/cost delta.

Out of scope: Full procurement automation, legal/vendor contracting, and on-prem deployment of the dashboard (this will be hosted internally behind SSO).
success_criteria: 1) Weekly churn score computed for 40 models with documented inputs and versioned formulas. 2) Dashboard used by at least 3 Product or Platform teams in the next 8 weeks for migration planning. 3) At least one proactive migration or purchase initiated because of an elevated risk signal within 12 weeks. 4) Mean time to remediate a model-availability incident reduced by 20% in the next quarter (measured by incident postmortems).
data_sources: internal usage telemetry (token volume, error rates)
methodology: Composite scoring model that blends: (A) availability signal (incident frequency, severity), (B) price momentum (3-month rolling repricing), (C) community velocity (open-source commit cadence, upstream maintainer signals), (D) contract risk (terms changes reported), and (E) substitutability score (feature/latency/cost distance to nearest compatible model). Each input normalized and weighted; weights tuned via retrospective on 6 historical model events. Weekly recalculation and provenance logging for audit.
deliverables: churn-score API (REST) with model_id and score history
technical design doc and weighting rationale (Confluence)

notes: Design constraint: Keep substitute suggestions conservative — only include models we've validated for API compatibility or for which we have a migration test template. Operational constraint: Scores will be advisory during pilot (no automated deprecation). Prioritization rule: emphasize churn signals for models with > 5% of total token spend across product teams.
